St. Silouan of Mount Athos

Saints

St. Silouan of Mount Athos

Period
1866–1938
Region
Mount Athos
Titles / vocation
Monastic
Commemoration
September 24

Introduction

The monastery account describes St. Silouan as a Russian peasant who became a monk at Saint Panteleimon's Monastery on Mount Athos. It emphasizes his long struggle, humility, prayer, and love for others. It identifies Sophrony as the disciple who preserved his life and writings and records Constantinople's glorification in 1988. The source is a monastery's biographical presentation, not St. Silouan's own surviving manuscript.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Silouan came from a Russian peasant family. His secular life included strenuous farm work and military service. The monastic account stresses the influence of his father’s uncomplicated faith and the tension between youthful passions and his wish to become a monk.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “peasant family”

Life and notable events

At Saint Panteleimon Monastery on Mount Athos he spent decades in ordinary monastic labor and prayer. His disciple Sophrony recorded a long inward struggle, including periods of desolation and the experience interpreted as a vision of Christ. Sophrony is the named transmitter of these recollections.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “Panteleimon”

Death and martyrdom

Silouan reposed at Saint Panteleimon Monastery on September 24, 1938. The commemoration records a monastic repose.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Published Saint Silouan account; repose

The published Athonite commemoration gives September 24,1938 for his repose. The commemoration identifies his burial at Saint Panteleimon Monastery.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Published Saint Silouan account; repose date

Writings and legacy

His disciple Sophrony edited Silouan’s writings and published a life with a collection of his teachings.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Published Saint Silouan account; writings and their editor
